57:1: Interpretation of Surat Al-Hadid Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn Abd Rabbih narrated to us, Baqiyah ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Bujayr ibn Sa’d narrated to me, on the authority of Khalid ibn Ma’dan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Bilal, on the authority of Irbadh ibn Sariyah, that he told them that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to recite the Tasbihat before going to sleep and he said: In them is a verse better than a thousand verses. This is how Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa’i narrated it through various chains of narration on the authority of Baqiyah. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan gharib. Al-Nasa’i narrated it on the authority of Ibn Abi Sarh, on the authority of Ibn Wahb, on the authority of Mu’awiyah ibn Salih, on the authority of Bujayr ibn Sa’d, on the authority of Khalid ibn Ma’dan, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) mentioned it as a mursal hadith, but he did not mention Abdullah ibn Abi Bilal or Irbadh ibn Sariyah. The verse referred to in the hadith is - and God knows best - His statement: He is the First and the Last, the Evident and the Immanent, and He is Knowing of all things, as will be explained shortly, God willing. In Him is the Trust and upon Him is reliance, and He is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful God the Almighty informs us that whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him, meaning animals and plants, as He said in another verse: “The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is therein glorify Him. And there is not a thing but glorifies Him with praise, but you do not understand their glorification. Indeed, He is Forbearing, Forgiving.” And His statement: And He is the Exalted in Might, meaning the One to whom everything submits, the Wise, in His creation, command, and law, “To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes death,” meaning He is the Owner who controls His creation, He gives life and causes death, and He gives whatever He wills. And He is over all things competent, meaning whatever He wills happens, and whatever He does not will does not happen. And His statement: He is the First and the Last, the Evident and the Immanent, is this verse referred to in the hadith of Irbad ibn Sariyah, that it is better than a thousand verses. Abu Dawud said: Abbas ibn Abd al-Azim narrated to us, al-Nadr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Ikrimah – meaning Ibn Ammar – narrated to us, Abu Zumail said: I asked Ibn Abbas, saying: What is that I find in my chest? He said: What is it? I said: By God, I will not speak about it. He said: He said to me: Something of doubt? He said and laughed. He said: No one was saved from that. He said: Until God Almighty revealed: “And if you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you, then ask those who have been reading the Scripture before you. The truth has certainly come to you from your Lord” verse. He said: And he said to me: If you find something in your soul, say: He is the First and the Last, the Evident and the Immanent, and He is Knowing of all things. The commentators have differed in their expressions and statements about this verse, with about a dozen opinions. Al-Bukhari said: Yahya said: The apparent is over all things in knowledge, and the hidden is over all things in knowledge. Our Sheikh Al-Hafiz Al-Mizzi said: This Yahya is Ibn Ziyad Al-Farra’. He has a book called The Meanings of the Qur’an. There are hadiths about this, including what Imam Ahmad said: Khalaf bin Al-Waleed told us, Ibn Ayyash told us, on the authority of Suhayl bin Abi Salih, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to supplicate when going to sleep: “O God, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the Mighty Throne, our Lord and Lord of all things, Revealer of the Torah, the Gospel, and the Criterion, Cleaver of the seed and the date stone. There is no god but You. I seek refuge in You from the evil of all things whose forelock You hold. You are the First, so there is nothing before You, and You are the Last, so there is nothing after You. You are the Manifest, so there is nothing above You, and You are the Hidden, so there is nothing beneath You. Pay off our debt and enrich us from poverty.” Muslim narrated it in his Sahih: Zuhair bin Harb told me, Jarir told us, on the authority of Sahl, who said: Abu Salih used to command us, when one of us wanted to sleep, to lie on his right side, then say: O God, Lord of the heavens, Lord of the earth, and Lord of the Mighty Throne, our Lord and Lord of all things, Cleaver of the seed and the date stone. And the Revealer of the Torah, the Gospel, and the Criterion, I seek refuge in You from the evil of every evil being, You hold its forelock. O God, You are the First, so there is nothing before You, and You are the Last, so there is nothing after You, and You are the Manifest, so there is nothing above You, and You are the Hidden, so there is nothing beneath You. Pay off our debts and enrich us from poverty. And he used to narrate this on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la al-Mawsili narrated something similar in his Musnad on the authority of Aisha, the Mother of the Believers, and he said: Uqba narrated to us, Yunus narrated to us, as-Sari ibn Ismail narrated to us, on the authority of al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Aisha, that she said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would order his bed to be spread out for him facing the Qiblah. When he lay down on it, he would put his right hand as a pillow, then he would whisper, not knowing what he was saying. When it was the last part of the night, he would raise his voice and say: O God, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the Mighty Throne, God of everything, and Revealer of the Torah, the Gospel, and the Criterion, Cleaver of the seed and the date stone. I seek refuge in You from the evil of everything, You hold its forelock. O God, You are the First, before whom there is nothing, and You are the Last, after whom there is nothing, and You are the Manifest, above whom there is nothing, and You are the Hidden, below whom there is nothing. Pay off our debt and enrich us from poverty. Al-Sari bin Ismail is the cousin of Al-Sha’bi, and he is very weak, and God knows best. Abu Isa Al-Tirmidhi said in his interpretation of this verse: Abd bin Hamid and others narrated to us, the meaning is the same. They said: Yunus bin Muhammad narrated to us, Shaiban bin Abd Al-Rahman narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: Al-Hasan narrated to us, from Abu Hurairah, who said: While the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was sitting with his companions, a cloud came over them. The Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Do you know what this is? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: These are the reins that irrigate the earth, driving it to a people who do not thank Him nor supplicate to Him. Then he said: Do you know what is above you? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: Indeed, it is the lofty, protected ceiling and its waves are restrained. Then he said: Do you know how much is between you and it? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: Between you and it are five hundred years. Then he said: Do you know what is above that? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: Above that is a heaven, between them is a journey of five hundred years - until he enumerated seven heavens - between every two heavens is like what is between the heaven and the earth. Then he said: Do you know what is above that? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: Above that is the Throne, and between it and the heaven is a distance like that between two heavens. Then he said: Do you know what is beneath you? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: It is the earth. Then he said: Do you know what is beneath that? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: Beneath it is another earth, between them is a journey of five hundred years - until he enumerated seven earths - between every two earths is a journey of five hundred years. Then he said: By the One in Whose Hand is the soul of Muhammad, if you were to lower a rope to the lowest earth, it would descend upon God. Then he recited: He is the First and the Last, the Evident and the Immanent, and He is Knowing of all things. Then Al-Tirmidhi said: This is a strange hadith from this source, and it is narrated on the authority of Ayoub and Yunus, meaning Ibn Ubayd, and Ali Ibn Zayd, and they said: Al-Hasan did not hear it from Abu Hurayrah. Some of the people of knowledge explained this hadith and said: He only descended with the knowledge, power, and authority of God, and the knowledge, power, and authority of God are in every place, and He is on the Throne, as He described in His Book. End quote. Imam Ahmad narrated this hadith on the authority of Surayj, on the authority of Al-Hakam ibn Abd Al-Malik, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him. He mentioned it while he had the distance between the two earths of a journey of seven hundred years. He said: If you were to lower one of you by a rope to the seventh lowest earth, he would descend to God. Then he recited: “He is the First and the Last, the Evident and the Immanent. And He is Knowing of all things.” Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Bazzar narrated it on the authority of Abu Ja`far Al-Razi, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Abu Hurairah. He mentioned the hadith, but Ibn Abi Hatim did not mention the end of it, which is his saying: If you were to lower yourself by a rope. He only said until he counted seven earths, between each two earths of a journey of five hundred years. Then he recited: “He is the First and the Last, the Evident and the Immanent. And He is Knowing of all things.” Al-Bazzar said: No one narrated it from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, except Abu Hurairah. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Bishr, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Sa`id, on the authority of Qatadah: He is the First and the Last, the Evident and the Immanent. He mentioned to us that while the Prophet of God, peace and blessings be upon him, was sitting with his companions, a cloud passed over them and he said: Do you know what this is? The hadith is mentioned in a similar context to that of al-Tirmidhi, except that it is mursal from this source, and perhaps this is the correct version, and God knows best. It has been narrated on the authority of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari may God be pleased with him, narrated by al-Bazzar in his Musnad and by al-Bayhaqi in Kitab al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat, but its chain of transmission is questionable and its text contains strangeness and oddity, and God knows best. Ibn Jarir said about the verse: And from the earth the like of them: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Four angels met between the heaven and the earth, and some of them said to each other: Where did you come from? One of them said: My Lord, the Almighty, sent me from the seventh heaven, and I left him there. The other said: My Lord, the Almighty, sent me from the seventh earth, and I left him there. The third said: My Lord sent me from the east, and I left him there. The third said: My Lord sent me from the west, and I left him there. This is a very strange hadith, and the first hadith may be attributed to Qatada, as narrated here from his statement, and God knows best.

57:7: God the Blessed and Most High has commanded us to believe in Him and His Messenger in the most perfect manner, and to be constant and steadfast in that and to continue. He has urged us to spend from what He has made you trustees over, that is, from what you have as a loan, because it was in the hands of those before you and then came to you. So God the Most High has guided us to use the money that you have been given as trustees in obeying Him. If you do so, then well and good, and if not, then He will hold you accountable for it and punish you for neglecting the duties in it. And His statement, of what He has made you trustees over indicates that it will be left behind for you, so perhaps your heir will obey God in it and be happier with what God has bestowed upon you than you, or he will disobey God in it and you will have sought to assist him in sin and aggression. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, I heard Qatadah narrating on the authority of Mutraf, meaning ibn `Abdullah ibn al-Shakheer, on the authority of his father, who said: I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, and he was saying: “You are distracted by multiplying. The son of Adam says, ‘My money, my money.’ Do you have any of your money except what you ate and finished, or wore out, or gave in charity and passed on?” Muslim narrated it on the authority of Shu`bah with the same chain of transmission, and he added: And everything else is gone and left to the people. God the Almighty says: Those among you who believe and spend will have a great reward. This encourages faith and spending in obedience. Then God the Almighty says: And what is the matter with you that you do not believe in God while the Messenger invites you to believe in your Lord? That is, what is preventing you from believing while the Messenger is among you, calling you to that and explaining to you the arguments and proofs for the truth of what he brought you? We have narrated in the hadith through various chains of transmission in the beginning of the explanation of the Book of Faith in Sahih al-Bukhari that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said one day to his companions: Which of the believers is most admirable to you in faith? They said: The angels. He said: And why do they not believe while they are with their Lord? They said: Then the prophets. He said: And why do they not believe while the revelation is being sent down to them? They said: So we are. He said: And why do you not believe while I am among you? But the most admirable of the believers in faith are people who come after you and find scriptures and believe in what is in them. We have mentioned part of this narration at the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah when God the Almighty says: Those who believe in the unseen. And the Almighty’s saying: And He has taken your covenant is like the Almighty’s saying: And remember the favor of God upon you and His covenant which He bound you when you said, ‘We hear and we obey.’ By that he means the pledge of allegiance to the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Jarir claimed that what is meant by that is the covenant that was taken from them in the loins of Adam, and this is the doctrine of Mujahid, and God knows best. And the Almighty said: It is He who sends down to His Servant clear signs meaning clear arguments, dazzling proofs, and conclusive evidence that He may bring you out from darkness into the light meaning from the darkness of ignorance, disbelief, and conflicting opinions to the light of guidance, certainty, and faith. And indeed, God is to you Most Kind and Most Merciful meaning in His sending down the Books and sending the Messengers to guide people, remove defects, and eliminate doubts. And when He first commanded them to believe and spend, then urged them to believe and made clear that He had removed its obstacles from them, He also urged them to spend, saying: And what is [the matter] with you that you should not spend in the cause of God while to God belongs the inheritance of the heavens and the earth? meaning, spend and do not fear poverty or scarcity, for the One in whose cause you have spent is the Owner of the heavens and the earth, and in His hand are their keys and with Him are their treasuries. He is the Owner of the Throne with all that it contains, and He is the One who says: And whatever you spend, He will replace it, and He is the Best of providers. He said: What you have will be exhausted, but what is with God is everlasting. So whoever puts his trust in God will spend and not fear any decrease from the Lord of the Throne, and he knows that God will replace it for him. And the Almighty said: Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought, meaning this is not equal to those who did not do as he did. That is because before the conquest of Mecca the situation was difficult, and no one believed at that time except the truthful ones. As for after the conquest, Islam appeared with a great appearance and people entered into the religion of God in multitudes. And for this reason God the Almighty said: “Those are greater in degree than those who spent afterward and fought. But to all God has promised good.” The majority of scholars agree that what is meant by conquest here is the conquest of Mecca. Al-Sha’bi and others said that what is meant by conquest here is the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. This opinion may be supported by what Imam Ahmad said: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Malik told us, Zuhair told us, Hamid al-Tawil told us, on the authority of Anas, who said: There was a conversation between Khalid ibn al-Walid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, and Khalid said to Abd al-Rahman: You are making things difficult for us by the days in which you have outstripped us. We were informed that this was mentioned to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Leave my companions alone, for by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, even if you spent gold equivalent to Mount Uhud or the mountains, you would not be able to reach their deeds. It is known that Khalid ibn al-Walid’s conversion to Islam, which was met with this address, was between the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah and the conquest of Mecca. This quarrel between them was in Banu Juthaymah, to whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had sent Khalid ibn al-Walid after the conquest. They kept saying: We have become Sabians, we have become Sabians, but they did not know how to say We have become Muslims, so Khalid ordered that they be killed and that those of them who were taken captive from them be killed. Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, Abdullah ibn Umar and others disagreed with him, so Khalid and Abd al-Rahman quarreled over that. What is in the Sahih is that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Do not insult my companions, for by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if one of you were to spend the equivalent of Mount Uhud in gold, it would not reach the level of one of them, or even half of it.” Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from the hadith of Ibn Wahb, who said: Hisham bin Saad told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Ata bin Yasar, on the authority of Abu Saeed Al-Khudri, that he said: We went out with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the year of Al-Hudaybiyyah, until when we were at Usfan, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Soon there will come a people whom you will consider your deeds insignificant compared to theirs. We said: Who are they, O Messenger of God? Are they Quraysh? He said: No, but the people of Yemen are more tender-hearted and soft-hearted. We said: Are they better than us, O Messenger of God? He said: “If one of them had a mountain of gold and spent it, it would not equal the measure of one of you, or even half of it. Indeed, this is the excess between us and the people. “Not equal among you are those who spent before the conquest and fought. Those are greater in degree than those who spent and fought afterwards. And to all God has promised good, and God is Acquainted with what you do.” This hadith is strange in this context. What is in the two Sahihs from the narration of a group on the authority of Ata’ ibn Yasar on the authority of Abu Sa’id is the mention of the Khawarij: “You will consider your prayers insignificant compared to their prayers and your fasting insignificant compared to their fasting. They will pass through the religion as an arrow passes through its target.” The hadith, but Ibn Jarir narrated this hadith from another chain of transmission. He said: Ibn al-Barqi told me, Ibn Abi Maryam told me, Muhammad ibn Ja’far told us, Zayd ibn Aslam told me on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Tammar on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: There will soon come a people whose deeds you will consider insignificant compared to their deeds. We said: Who are they, O Messenger of God? Quraysh? He said: No, but the people of Yemen are the most tender-hearted and soft-hearted. He pointed to Yemen and said: "They are the people of Yemen. 57:12: God Almighty says, informing us about the faithful who give charity, that on the Day of Resurrection, their light will run before them in the arenas of the Resurrection, according to their deeds, as Abdullah bin Masoud said in his statement, God Almighty: Their light will run before them, he said: According to the extent of their deeds, they will pass over the Sirat. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir, and Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say, “Among the believers are those whose light will shine from Medina to Aden, Abyan, and Sana’a, and even less than that, until among the believers are those whose light will shine where their feet stand.” Sufyan al-Thawri said, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Junada bin Abi Umayya, who said: You are written with God by your names, your features, your rituals, your private conversations, and your gatherings. Ad-Dahhak said: “There is no one who will not be given light on the Day of Resurrection. When they reach the Sirat, the light of the hypocrites will be extinguished. When the believers saw that, they feared that their light would be extinguished as the light of the hypocrites was extinguished, so they said: ‘Our Lord, perfect our light for us.’” Al-Hasan said: Their light will run before them, meaning on the Sirat. I will look in front of me and behind me, to my right and to my left, and I will recognize my nation from among the nations.” A man said to him: O Prophet of God, how will you recognize your nation from among the nations between Noah and your nation? He said: I recognize them with limbs marked by the traces of ablution, and no other nation will have them, and I recognize them when they will be given their books. I know them by their right hands, I know them by their marks on their faces, and I know them by their light running before them. And His statement, and in their right hands, Ad-Dahhak said, meaning, and in their right hands is their book, as He said, So whoever is given his book in his right hand, and His statement, “Good tidings to you this Day: gardens beneath which rivers flow,” meaning He said to them: Good tidings to you this Day: gardens, meaning, for you is the good tidings of gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein meaning, remaining therein forever. That is the great attainment. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abdah bin Sulayman told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, Safwan bin Amr told us, Salim bin Amir told me: We went out to a funeral procession at the gate of Damascus, and with us was Abu Umamah al-Bahili. When the funeral prayer was offered and they began to bury it, Abu Umamah said: O people, you have now become and spent the evening in a house in which you divide the good and bad deeds, and you are about to move from it to another house, which is this one - pointing to the grave - the house of solitude, the house of darkness, the house of worms, and the house of constriction, except for what God has expanded. Then you will move from it to the places of the Day of Resurrection. You will be in some of those places until a command from God overwhelms the people, so some faces will turn white and some will turn black. Then you will move from it to another house, and severe darkness will overwhelm the people. Then the light will be divided, and the believer will be given light, while the disbeliever and the hypocrite will be left, and they will not be given anything. This is the example that God, the Most High, gave in His Book, when He said: Or [like] darknesses within a deep sea, which is covered by waves, above which are waves, above which are clouds - darknesses, one upon another. If he puts out his hand, he can hardly see it. And he to whom God has not given light - for him there is no light. The disbeliever and the hypocrite will not be illuminated by the light of the believer, just as the blind man is not illuminated by the sight of the seeing man. And the hypocrites, men and women, will say to the believers, Wait for us, that we may take from your light. It will be said, Go back behind you and seek light. This is the trick of God with which He deceives the hypocrites, as He said, They seek to deceive God, but He will deceive them. So they return to the place where the light was divided, but they do not find anything. So they turn back to them, and a wall has been set up between them, with a gate, within which is mercy, but outside of it is punishment. Sulaym ibn Amir said: The hypocrite will continue to be deceived until the light is divided and God distinguishes between the hypocrite and the believer. Then he said: My father told us, Yahya ibn Uthman told us, Ibn Haywah told us, Artah ibn al-Mundhir told us, Yusuf ibn al-Hajjaj told us on the authority of Abu Umamah who said: God will send darkness on the Day of Resurrection and no believer or disbeliever will see his hand until God sends light to the believers according to their deeds. The hypocrites will follow them and say, Wait for us so that we may take from your light. Al-Awfi, Al-Dahhak and others said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: While the people were in darkness, God sent a light. When the believers saw the light, they headed towards it. The light was a guide from God to Paradise. When the hypocrites saw the believers depart, they followed them, so God made the hypocrites dark. They then said, Wait for us so that we may take from your light, for we were with you in the world. The believers will say, Go back behind you, from where you came from the darkness and seek the light there. When they have completed their entry, the gate will be closed, and the hypocrites will remain behind it in confusion, darkness, and torment, as they were in this world in disbelief, ignorance, doubt, and confusion. They will call out to them, Were we not with you? That is, the hypocrites will call out to the believers, "Were we not with you in this world? Were we not with you in this world, attending the Friday prayers with you, praying with you in congregation, standing with you at Arafat, attending the battles with you, and performing all the other duties with you?" They will say, Yes. That is, the believers will answer the hypocrites, saying, "Yes, you were with us. But you tempted yourselves and waited and doubted, and false desires deceived you." Some of the early Muslims said, That is, you tempted yourselves with pleasures, sins, and desires, and you waited, that is, you delayed repentance from one time to another. Qatada said: You waited for the truth and its people, and you doubted that is, the resurrection after death, and your wishful thinking deceived you that is, you said, We will be forgiven. It was also said that the world deceived you until the command of God came that is, you continued in this until death came to you, and the Deceiver deceived you about God that is, Satan. Qatada said: They were deceived by Satan, and by God, they continued to be deceived until God threw them into the Fire. The meaning of these words of the believers to the hypocrites is that you were with us, that is, with bodies that had no intention or hearts with them, but you were only in confusion and doubt, so you were showing off to people and you did not remember God except a little. Mujahid said: The hypocrites were with the believers while they were alive, marrying them, cheating on them, and socializing with them, and they were with them while they were dead and they would all be given the light on the Day of Resurrection, and the light would be extinguished from the hypocrites when they reached the wall, and they would be distinguished from each other at that time. They will be in gardens, asking one another about the criminals. “What has brought you into Hellfire?” They will say, We were not of those who prayed, nor did we feed the poor, and we used to converse with those who converse, and we used to deny the Day of Judgment until the certainty came to us. This only came from them as a rebuke and rebuke. Then God the Most High said: So what benefit will the intercession of intercessors be to them? Just as He said here: So today no ransom will be taken from you, nor from those who disbelieved. That is, if one of you came today with the earth full of gold and as much with it to ransom himself from the punishment of God, it would not be accepted. God the Most High says: Your refuge is the Fire, meaning it is your destination and to it you will return. God the Most High says: It is your protector, meaning it is more deserving of you than any other abode, based on your disbelief and doubt. What an evil destination!

It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir, and Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say, “Among the believers are those whose light will shine from Medina to Aden, Abyan, and Sana’a, and even less than that, until among the believers are those whose light will shine where their feet stand.” Sufyan al-Thawri said, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Junada bin Abi Umayya, who said: You are written with God by your names, your features, your rituals, your private conversations, and your gatherings. So when the Day of Resurrection comes, it will be said: O so-and-so, this is…” Your light, so-and-so, you have no light, and he read, Their light runs before them. Ad-Dahhak said: “There is no one who will not be given light on the Day of Resurrection. When they reach the Sirat, the light of the hypocrites will be extinguished. When the believers saw that, they feared that their light would be extinguished as the light of the hypocrites was extinguished, so they said: ‘Our Lord, perfect our light for us.’” Al-Hasan said: Their light will run before them, meaning on the Sirat. Ibn Abi Hatim, may God have mercy on him, said: Abu Ubaidullah, the nephew of Ibn Wahb, told us, my uncle told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Habib, on the authority of Saeed ibn Masoud, that he heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr narrating, that he heard Abu al-Darda’ and Abu Dharr narrating on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “I will be the first to be given permission on the Day of Resurrection to prostrate, and the first to be given permission to raise his head. I will look in front of me and behind me, to my right and to my left, and I will recognize my nation from among the nations.” A man said to him: O Prophet of God, how will you recognize your nation from among the nations between Noah and your nation? He said: I recognize them with limbs marked by the traces of ablution, and no other nation will have them, and I recognize them when they will be given their books. I know them by their right hands, I know them by their marks on their faces, and I know them by their light running before them. And His statement, and in their right hands, Ad-Dahhak said, meaning, and in their right hands is their book, as He said, So whoever is given his book in his right hand, and His statement, “Good tidings to you this Day: gardens beneath which rivers flow,” meaning He said to them: Good tidings to you this Day: gardens, meaning, for you is the good tidings of gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein meaning, remaining therein forever. That is the great attainment. And His statement, The Day the hypocrites, men and women, will say to those who have believed, ‘Wait for us so that we may take from your light,’ This is report from the Most High about what will happen on the Day of Resurrection in the gathering places of disturbing terrors, great earthquakes, and terrible matters, and that no one will be saved on that Day except he who believes in God and His Messenger and does what God has commanded and leaves what He has forbidden. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abdah bin Sulayman told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, Safwan bin Amr told us, Salim bin Amir told me: We went out to a funeral procession at the gate of Damascus, and with us was Abu Umamah al-Bahili. When the funeral prayer was offered and they began to bury it, Abu Umamah said: O people, you have now become and spent the evening in a house in which you divide the good and bad deeds, and you are about to move from it to another house, which is this one - pointing to the grave - the house of solitude, the house of darkness, the house of worms, and the house of constriction, except for what God has expanded. Then you will move from it to the places of the Day of Resurrection. You will be in some of those places until a command from God overwhelms the people, so some faces will turn white and some will turn black. Then you will move from it to another house, and severe darkness will overwhelm the people. Then the light will be divided, and the believer will be given light, while the disbeliever and the hypocrite will be left, and they will not be given anything. This is the example that God, the Most High, gave in His Book, when He said: Or [like] darknesses within a deep sea, which is covered by waves, above which are waves, above which are clouds - darknesses, one upon another. If he puts out his hand, he can hardly see it. And he to whom God has not given light - for him there is no light. The disbeliever and the hypocrite will not be illuminated by the light of the believer, just as the blind man is not illuminated by the sight of the seeing man. And the hypocrites, men and women, will say to the believers, Wait for us, that we may take from your light. It will be said, Go back behind you and seek light. This is the trick of God with which He deceives the hypocrites, as He said, They seek to deceive God, but He will deceive them. So they return to the place where the light was divided, but they do not find anything. So they turn back to them, and a wall has been set up between them, with a gate, within which is mercy, but outside of it is punishment. Sulaym ibn Amir said: The hypocrite will continue to be deceived until the light is divided and God distinguishes between the hypocrite and the believer. Then he said: My father told us, Yahya ibn Uthman told us, Ibn Haywah told us, Artah ibn al-Mundhir told us, Yusuf ibn al-Hajjaj told us on the authority of Abu Umamah who said: God will send darkness on the Day of Resurrection and no believer or disbeliever will see his hand until God sends light to the believers according to their deeds. The hypocrites will follow them and say, Wait for us so that we may take from your light. Al-Awfi, Al-Dahhak and others said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: While the people were in darkness, God sent a light. When the believers saw the light, they headed towards it. The light was a guide from God to Paradise. When the hypocrites saw the believers depart, they followed them, so God made the hypocrites dark. They then said, Wait for us so that we may take from your light, for we were with you in the world. The believers will say, Go back behind you, from where you came from the darkness and seek the light there. Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Al-Hasan ibn Arfa ibn Alawiya al-Qattan told us, Ismail ibn Isa al-Attar told us, Ishaq ibn Bishr ibn Hudhayfah told us, Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God Almighty will call people on the Day of Resurrection by their names as a cover from Him for His servants. As for at the Bridge, God Almighty will give every believer a light and every hypocrite a light. When they are all lined up on the Bridge, God will take away the light of the hypocrites, men and women. The hypocrites will say, ‘Wait for us, that we may borrow from your light.’ The believers will say, ‘Our Lord, perfect our light for us.’ Then no one will remember anyone else at that time.” God the Almighty said: And a wall will be placed between them, having a gate; within it is mercy, but outside of it is punishment. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: It is a wall between Paradise and Hellfire. Abdur-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: It is the one about whom God the Almighty said: And between them is a veil. This is how it was narrated from Mujahid may God have mercy on him and others, and this is the correct view. Within it is mercy, meaning Paradise and what is in it. And outside of it is punishment, meaning Hellfire. This was said by Qatadah, Ibn Zayd, and others. Ibn Jarir said: It has been said that this wall is the wall of Jerusalem near the Valley of Hellfire. Then he said: Ibn al-Barqi told us, Amr ibn Abi Salamah told us, on the authority of Saeed ibn Atiyyah ibn Qays, on the authority of Abu al-Awwam, the muezzin of Jerusalem, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Amr say: The wall mentioned by God in the Qur’an: And a wall will be placed between them, having a gate; within it is mercy, but outside of it is punishment, is the eastern wall, inside of which is the mosque and what is next to it, and outside of which is the Valley of Hellfire. Then it was narrated from Ubadah ibn al-Samit, Ka’b al-Ahbar, and Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin something similar to this. This is attributed to them as meaning that they intended by this to approximate the meaning and give an example of it, not that this is what is intended by the Qur’an: this specific wall itself, the mosque itself, and the valley beyond it known as the Valley of Hell, for Paradise is in the heavens in the highest of the high, and Hell is in the lowest of the low. Ka’b al-Ahbar’s saying that the gate mentioned in the Qur’an is the Gate of Mercy, which is one of the gates of the mosque, this is from his Isra’iliyyat and nonsense. Rather, what is meant by this is the wall that will be set up on the Day of Resurrection to separate the believers from the hypocrites. When the believers reach it, they will enter it from its gate. When they have completed their entry, the gate will be closed, and the hypocrites will remain behind it in confusion, darkness, and torment, as they were in this world in disbelief, ignorance, doubt, and confusion. They will call out to them, Were we not with you? That is, the hypocrites will call out to the believers, "Were we not with you in this world? Were we not with you in this world, attending the Friday prayers with you, praying with you in congregation, standing with you at Arafat, attending the battles with you, and performing all the other duties with you?" They will say, Yes. That is, the believers will answer the hypocrites, saying, "Yes, you were with us. But you tempted yourselves and waited and doubted, and false desires deceived you." Some of the early Muslims said, That is, you tempted yourselves with pleasures, sins, and desires, and you waited, that is, you delayed repentance from one time to another. Qatada said: You waited for the truth and its people, and you doubted that is, the resurrection after death, and your wishful thinking deceived you that is, you said, We will be forgiven. It was also said that the world deceived you until the command of God came that is, you continued in this until death came to you, and the Deceiver deceived you about God that is, Satan. Qatada said: They were deceived by Satan, and by God, they continued to be deceived until God threw them into the Fire. The meaning of these words of the believers to the hypocrites is that you were with us, that is, with bodies that had no intention or hearts with them, but you were only in confusion and doubt, so you were showing off to people and you did not remember God except a little. Mujahid said: The hypocrites were with the believers while they were alive, marrying them, cheating on them, and socializing with them, and they were with them while they were dead and they would all be given the light on the Day of Resurrection, and the light would be extinguished from the hypocrites when they reached the wall, and they would be distinguished from each other at that time. This statement of the believers does not contradict their statement, which God the Most High has informed us about them, where He says, and He is the most truthful of speakers: “Every soul will be a pledge for what it has earned, Except the companions of the right hand. They will be in gardens, asking one another about the criminals. “What has brought you into Hellfire?” They will say, We were not of those who prayed, nor did we feed the poor, and we used to converse with those who converse, and we used to deny the Day of Judgment until the certainty came to us. This only came from them as a rebuke and rebuke. Then God the Most High said: So what benefit will the intercession of intercessors be to them? Just as He said here: So today no ransom will be taken from you, nor from those who disbelieved. That is, if one of you came today with the earth full of gold and as much with it to ransom himself from the punishment of God, it would not be accepted. God the Most High says: Your refuge is the Fire, meaning it is your destination and to it you will return. God the Most High says: It is your protector, meaning it is more deserving of you than any other abode, based on your disbelief and doubt. What an evil destination!

57:16: God the Almighty says: Has not the time come for the believers that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of God? That is, they should soften when reminded, preached, and heard the Quran, so that they should understand it, submit to it, listen to it, and obey it. Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: Saleh al-Mari told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said: God felt slow in the hearts of the believers, so He admonished them thirteen days after the revelation of the Quran, saying: Has not the time come for those who have believed that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of God? The verse was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabah, on the authority of Husayn al-Marwazi, on the authority of Ibn al-Mubarak, with this chain of transmission. Then he and Muslim said: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Amr bin Al-Harith told me, on the authority of Sa’id bin Abi Hilal, meaning Al-Laithi, on the authority of Awn bin Abdullah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, who said: There were only four years between our conversion to Islam and the time when God admonished us with this verse, Has not the time come for those who have believed that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of God? This is how Muslim narrated it at the end of the book, and An-Nasa’i included it in his commentary on this verse on the authority of Harun bin Sa’id Al-Ayli, on the authority of Ibn Wahb. Ibn Majah narrated it on the authority of Musa bin Ya’qub Az-Zama’i, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Amir bin Abdullah bin Az-Zubayr, on the authority of his father, similarly, so he included it in the Musnad of Ibn Az-Zubayr. However, Al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad on the authority of Musa bin Ya’qub, on the authority of Abu Hazim, on the authority of Amir, on the authority of Ibn Az-Zubayr, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, and he mentioned it. Sufyan al-Thawri said, on the authority of al-Mas’udi, on the authority of al-Qasim, who said: The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, became tired of a religion and said: Tell us, O Messenger of God. So God, the Most High, revealed: We narrate to you the best of stories. He said: Then they became tired of a religion and said: Tell us, O Messenger of God. So God, the Most High, revealed: God has sent down the best of statements. Then they became tired of a religion and said: Tell us, O Messenger of God. So God, the Most High, revealed: Has not the time come for those who have believed that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of God? Qatada said: Has not the time come for those who have believed that their hearts should become humbly submissive at the remembrance of God? It was mentioned to us that Shaddad ibn Aws used to narrate on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: The first thing that will be lifted up from people is humility. God the Almighty said: And do not be like those who were given the Scripture before, and a long period passed over them and their hearts hardened. God the Almighty forbade the believers from imitating those who were given the Scripture before them, from the Jews and Christians. When a long period passed over them, they changed the Book of God that was in their hands and bought with it a small price and threw it behind their backs. They turned to different opinions and fabricated sayings, and imitated men in the religion of God and took their rabbis and monks as lords besides God. At that time, their hearts hardened, so they do not accept admonition, nor do their hearts soften with a promise or a threat. And many of them are wicked, that is, in their deeds, so their hearts are corrupt and their deeds are invalid, as God the Almighty said: “So because they broke their covenant, We cursed them and made their hearts hard. They distort words from their [proper] usages and forgot a portion of that of which they were reminded.” That is, their hearts became corrupt and hardened, and it became their nature to distort words from their [proper] usages, and they abandoned the deeds that they were commanded to do and committed what they were forbidden to do. On his authority, and for this reason God forbade the believers from imitating them in any of the basic and secondary matters. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Hisham bin Ammar told us, Shihab bin Kharash told us, Hajjaj bin Dinar told us, on the authority of Mansur bin Al-Mu’tamir, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Umaila Al-Fazari, who said: Abdullah bin Mas’ud told us a hadith that I have never heard more wonderful than it, except for something from the Book of God or something that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the time had passed for the Children of Israel and their hearts had hardened, they invented a book from themselves that their hearts were attracted to, their tongues deemed permissible and found delicious, and the truth was standing between them and many of their desires. So they said, ‘Come, let us call the Children of Israel to this book of ours. Whoever follows us in it, we will leave him, and whoever does not like to follow us, we will kill him.’ So they did that, and among them was a jurist. 57:18: God the Almighty tells us how He will reward those who give charity, both men and women, with their money from those in need, poverty, and destitution. And lend God a good loan, meaning they give it with a sincere intention, seeking God’s pleasure, not seeking any reward or thanks from the one who gave it. That is why He said, It will be multiplied for them, meaning He will reward them tenfold for their good deed, and it will be increased to seven hundred times that, and above that, and for them is a noble reward, meaning a generous and good reward, a righteous destination, and a noble final destination. God the Almighty says, And those who believe in God and His messengers—those are the truthful. This completes the description of the believers in God and His messengers as truthful. Al-Awfi said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding God the Almighty’s saying, And those who believe in God and His messengers—those are the truthful, this is separate. And the martyrs are with their Lord; they will have their reward and their light. Abu al-Dhaha said, Those are the truthful. Then He resumed speaking and said, And the martyrs are with their Lord. This is what Masruq, al-Dahhak, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and others said. Al-A’mash said, on the authority of Abu Ad-Dahha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, regarding the words of God Almighty, Those are the truthful and the martyrs with their Lord, he said: They are three types: meaning the truthful, the truthful, and the martyrs, as God Almighty said: And whoever obeys God and the Messenger - those will be with those upon whom God has bestowed favor of the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous. So He distinguished between the truthful and the martyrs, indicating that they are two types, and there is no doubt that the truthful is of a higher status than the martyr, as Imam Malik bin Anas, may God have mercy on him, narrated in his book Al-Muwatta’, on the authority of Safwan bin Sulaym, on the authority of Ata’ bin Yasar, on the authority of Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The people of Paradise will see the people of the chambers above them as you see a shining star setting in the horizon from the east or the west, because of the difference between them. He said: O Messenger of God, those are the stations of the prophets, and no one else will reach them. He said: Yes, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, they are men who believed in God and believed in the messengers. Al-Bukhari and Muslim agreed to narrate it from the hadith of Malik with it. Others said: Rather, what is meant by his words God the Almighty said: Those are the truthful and the martyrs with their Lord. So He informed about the believers in God and His messengers that they are the truthful and the martyrs. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Mujahid. Then Ibn Jarir said: Salih bin Harb Abu Muammar told me, Ismail bin Yahya told us, Ibn Ajlan told us, on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, on the authority of Al-Bara’ bin Azib, who said: I heard the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, say: The believers of my nation are martyrs. Then the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, recited this verse: And those who have believed in God and His messengers - those are the truthful and the martyrs with their Lord. This is a strange hadith. Abu Ishaq said on the authority of Amr bin Maymun regarding God’s statement: “And those who have believed in God and His messengers - those are the truthful and the martyrs with their Lord. They will have their reward and their light,” he said: They will come on the Day of Resurrection together like two fingers. And the Almighty’s saying: And the martyrs are with their Lord meaning in the Gardens of Bliss, as it came in the two Sahihs: “The souls of the martyrs are in the crops of green birds that roam in Paradise wherever they wish, then they take refuge in those lamps. Then your Lord looked at them and said: What do you want? They said: We would like you to return us to this worldly home so that we can fight for You and be killed as we were killed the first time. Then He said: I have decreed that they will not return to it.” And the Almighty said: For them is their reward and their light meaning for them is a great reward with God and a great light that runs before them, and in that they vary according to the deeds they did in this world, as Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Ishaq told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Ata’ bin Dinar, on the authority of Abu Yazid Al-Khawlani, who said: I heard Fadalah bin Ubaid say: I heard Umar bin Al-Khattab say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “The martyrs are four: a believing man with good faith who encountered the enemy and believed in God and was killed. That is the one whom people look at like this,” and he raised his head until the cap of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the cap of Umar fell off. “The second is a believer who encountered the enemy and it was as if his back was struck with thorns of the acacia tree, and an arrow struck him and killed him. That is in the second degree. The third is a believing man who mixed good deeds with bad ones. He encountered the enemy and believed in God until he was killed. That is in the third degree. The fourth is a believing man who was very extravagant with himself. He encountered the enemy and believed in God until he was killed. That is the one whom people look at like this.” And he raised his head until the cap of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, fell off. “The second is a believer who encountered the enemy and it was as if his back was struck with the thorns of the acacia tree, and an arrow struck him and killed him. That is in the second degree.” And the third is a believing man who mixed good deeds with bad deeds. He encountered the enemy and believed in God until he was killed. That is in the third degree. And the fourth is a believing man who was very extravagant with himself. He encountered the enemy and believed in God until he was killed. That is in the fourth degree.” And thus it was narrated by Ali bin Al-Madini on the authority of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi on the authority of Ibn al-Mubarak on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah, and he said: This is a valid Egyptian chain of transmission. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah, and he said: It is good and rare. And the Almighty’s statement: And those who disbelieve and deny Our signs - those are the companions of Hellfire, when He mentioned the happy ones and their final destination, He followed it with mentioning the wretched ones and explaining their condition.

57:20: God Almighty says, belittling and belittling the life of this world: The life of this world is only play and amusement, adornment and boasting to one another and competition in increase of wealth and children. That is, this is the essence of its situation for its people, as God Almighty says: “Beautified for people is the love of desires - of women and children, and heaped-up sums of gold and silver, and branded horses, and livestock and tillage. That is the enjoyment of worldly life, and God has with Him the best return.” Then God Almighty gave an example of worldly life in that it is a fleeting flower and a passing blessing, saying: like the example of rain, which is the rain that comes after people have despaired, as God Almighty says: And it is He who sends down rain after they have despaired. And the Almighty said: The disbelievers are amazed by its growth, meaning the farmers are amazed by the growth of that crop that grew with rain. Just as the farmers are amazed by that, so too the life of this world amazes the disbelievers, for they are the most eager for it and the most inclined towards it. Then it withers and you see it yellow, then it becomes debris, meaning that the crop withers and you see it yellow after it was green and fresh, then after all of that it becomes debris, meaning it becomes dry and shattered. This is how the life of this world is: first young, then mature, then old and ugly. Man is like this in the prime of his life and the prime of his youth, fresh, tender, soft, and beautiful in appearance. Then he begins to reach middle age, so his nature changes and he loses some of his strength. Then he grows up and becomes an old man, weak in strength, with little movement, unable to do anything, as the Almighty said: “God is He who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness and gray hair. He creates what He wills, and He is the Knowing, the Competent.” And since this example indicates the passing of this world, Its expiration and emptiness are inevitable, and the Hereafter is bound to happen. He warned against its matter and desired what is good in it, saying: “And in the Hereafter is severe punishment and forgiveness from God and approval. And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion.” That is, there is nothing in the Hereafter that is coming and near except either this or that: either severe punishment, or forgiveness from God and approval. God the Almighty said: And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion. That is, it is an enjoyment that will make those who rely on it jealous, for they will be deceived by it and will become arrogant to the point that they believe that there is no home other than it and no place to return after it. It is insignificant and small in comparison to the home of the Hereafter. Ibn Jarir said: Ali ibn Harb al-Mawsili told us, al-Maharbi told us, Muhammad ibn Amr told us, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “The space of a whip in Paradise is better than this world and whatever is in it. Recite: ‘And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion.’” This hadith is authentic in Sahih without this addition, and God knows best. Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numayr and Waki’ both told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Shaqiq, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Paradise is nearer to any one of you than the strap of his sandal, and the Fire is likewise. Al-Bukhari alone transmitted it in his chapter on asceticism, from the hadith of al-Thawri, on the authority of al-A’mash. This hadith is evidence of the proximity of good and evil to man. If this is the case, then God the Almighty urged him to hasten to do good deeds, perform acts of obedience and leave forbidden things, which will expiate his sins and mistakes and bring him reward and degrees. God the Almighty said: Race one another to forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise as wide as the heavens and earth. What is meant is the type of heaven and earth, as God the Almighty said in another verse: And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise as wide as the heavens and earth, prepared for the righteous. And He said here: “Prepared for those who believe in God and His messengers. That is the bounty of God. He bestows it upon whom He wills, and God is the possessor of great bounty.” That is, what God has qualified them for is from His bounty, favor, and kindness to them, as we mentioned earlier in the Sahih that the poor emigrants said: O Messenger of God, the wealthy have taken the rewards, the highest degrees, and the everlasting bliss. He said: And what is that? They said: They pray as we pray, they fast as we fast, they give in charity but we do not give in charity, they free slaves but we do not free slaves. He said: “Shall I not guide you to something which, if you do it, will make you precede those who come after you, and no one will be better than you except the one who does as you do: glorify, magnify and praise God thirty-three times after every prayer.” He said: So they returned and said: Our wealthy brothers heard what we did and did the same. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: That is the bounty of God which He gives to whomever He wills.

Just as the farmers are amazed by that, so too the life of this world amazes the disbelievers, for they are the most eager for it and the most inclined towards it. Then it withers and you see it yellow, then it becomes debris, meaning that the crop withers and you see it yellow after it was green and fresh, then after all of that it becomes debris, meaning it becomes dry and shattered. This is how the life of this world is: first young, then mature, then old and ugly. Man is like this in the prime of his life and the prime of his youth, fresh, tender, soft, and beautiful in appearance. Then he begins to reach middle age, so his nature changes and he loses some of his strength. Then he grows up and becomes an old man, weak in strength, with little movement, unable to do anything, as the Almighty said: “God is He who created you from weakness, then made after weakness strength, then made after strength weakness and gray hair. He creates what He wills, and He is the Knowing, the Competent.” And since this example indicates the passing of this world, Its expiration and emptiness are inevitable, and the Hereafter is bound to happen. He warned against its matter and desired what is good in it, saying: “And in the Hereafter is severe punishment and forgiveness from God and approval. And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion.” That is, there is nothing in the Hereafter that is coming and near except either this or that: either severe punishment, or forgiveness from God and approval. God the Almighty said: And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion. That is, it is an enjoyment that will make those who rely on it jealous, for they will be deceived by it and will become arrogant to the point that they believe that there is no home other than it and no place to return after it. It is insignificant and small in comparison to the home of the Hereafter. Ibn Jarir said: Ali ibn Harb al-Mawsili told us, al-Maharbi told us, Muhammad ibn Amr told us, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “The space of a whip in Paradise is better than this world and whatever is in it. Recite: ‘And the life of this world is nothing but the enjoyment of delusion.’” This hadith is authentic in Sahih without this addition, and God knows best. Imam Ahmad said: Ibn Numayr and Waki’ both told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Shaqiq, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Paradise is nearer to any one of you than the strap of his sandal, and the Fire is likewise. Al-Bukhari alone transmitted it in his chapter on asceticism, from the hadith of al-Thawri, on the authority of al-A’mash. This hadith is evidence of the proximity of good and evil to man. If this is the case, then God the Almighty urged him to hasten to do good deeds, perform acts of obedience and leave forbidden things, which will expiate his sins and mistakes and bring him reward and degrees. God the Almighty said: Race one another to forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise as wide as the heavens and earth. What is meant is the type of heaven and earth, as God the Almighty said in another verse: And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise as wide as the heavens and earth, prepared for the righteous. And He said here: “Prepared for those who believe in God and His messengers. That is the bounty of God. He bestows it upon whom He wills, and God is the possessor of great bounty.” That is, what God has qualified them for is from His bounty, favor, and kindness to them, as we mentioned earlier in the Sahih that the poor emigrants said: O Messenger of God, the wealthy have taken the rewards, the highest degrees, and the everlasting bliss. He said: And what is that? They said: They pray as we pray, they fast as we fast, they give in charity but we do not give in charity, they free slaves but we do not free slaves. He said: “Shall I not guide you to something which, if you do it, will make you precede those who come after you, and no one will be better than you except the one who does as you do: glorify, magnify and praise God thirty-three times after every prayer.” He said: So they returned and said: Our wealthy brothers heard what we did and did the same. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: That is the bounty of God which He gives to whomever He wills.
57:22: God the Almighty informs us of His previous decree in His creation before He created the world, saying: No disaster strikes upon the earth or among yourselves except that it is in a register before We bring it into existence meaning before We create the creation and bring the soul into existence. Some of them said: Before We bring it into existence refers to the souls. It was also said: “It refers to the disaster, but it is better to refer it to creation and the world because the statement indicates them, as Ibn Jarir said: Ya’qub told me, Ibn Ulayyah told me on the authority of Mansur ibn Abd al-Rahman who said: I was sitting with al-Hasan and a man said, “Ask him about the statement of God the Almighty: “No disaster strikes upon the earth or among yourselves except that it is in a register before We bring it into existence” So I asked him about it and he said: Glory be to God, and who doubts this? Every disaster between the heaven and the earth is in the Book of God before He brings the soul into existence. Qatada said: Whatever calamity befalls the earth he said: It is the years meaning the drought nor in yourselves meaning: the pains and diseases. He said: It has reached us that no one is afflicted with a scratch from a stick, a foot injury, or a vein rupture except for a sin, and what God forgives is greater. This great and noble verse is one of the clearest proofs against the Qadarites, who deny foreknowledge - may God curse them. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Abd al-Rahman told us, Haywah and Ibn Lahi'ah told us: Abu Hani' al-Khawlani told us that he heard Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hubli say: I heard Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-'As say: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: God decreed the destinies fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth. Muslim narrated it in his Sahih from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Wahb, Haywah ibn Shuraih, and Nafi' ibn Zayd, all three of them from Abu Hani' with this chain of narration. Ibn Wahb added: and His Throne was over the water. At-Tirmidhi narrated it and said: It is hasan sahih. God the Almighty said: That, for God, is easy means that His knowledge of things before they come into being and His writing them down in accordance with what will occur at the time is easy for God the Almighty, because He knows what has been and what will be, and what would not have been, how it would have been. God the Almighty says: {So that you may not grieve over what has escaped you or exult over what He has given you} meaning, We informed you of Our advanced knowledge and predestination of things before they came into being, and of Our predestination of all things before they came into existence, so that you may know that what befell you could not have missed you and what missed you could not have befallen you. So do not grieve over what has escaped you because if something had been predestined, it would have come to pass. {And do not rejoice over what He has given you} meaning, it came to you. The interpretation of gave you means gave you, and both are intertwined, meaning, do not boast to people about what God has bestowed upon you, because that is not due to your own effort or toil, but rather it is due to God’s decree and provision for you. So do not take God’s blessings as a means of evil and arrogance, boasting about them to people. For this reason, God the Almighty says: {And God does not like any self-deluded boaster} meaning, one who is self-deluded and proud, that is, over others. Ikrimah said: There is no one who rejoices and grieves except Him, but make joy gratitude and sadness patience. Then God Almighty said: Those who are stingy and enjoin stinginess on people meaning they do evil and urge people to do it. And whoever turns away meaning from God’s command and obedience to Him, then indeed, God is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy as Moses, peace be upon him, said: If you disbelieve, you and whoever is on the earth entirely, then indeed, God is Free of need, Praiseworthy.
