57:25: God Almighty says: Indeed, We sent Our messengers with clear proofs, meaning miracles, dazzling arguments, and conclusive evidence, and sent down with them the Book, which is the true transmission, and the Balance, which is justice, as Mujahid, Qatadah, and others said. It is the truth to which sound, upright minds testify, opposing unsound opinions, as God Almighty said: Is one who is on clear evidence from his Lord, and a witness from Him recites it? And God Almighty said: The nature of God upon which He created mankind. And God Almighty said: And the heaven He raised and set up the Balance. That is why He said in this verse: That people may maintain justice, meaning with truth and justice, which is following the messengers in what they informed them of and obeying them in what they commanded them to do. For what they brought is the truth beyond which there is no truth, as He said: And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice, meaning truth in the report and justice in the commands and prohibitions. That is why the believers say when they occupy the rooms of Paradise, the lofty dwellings, and the arranged thrones, Praise be to God who has guided us to this, and we were not… We would not have been guided if God had not guided us. The messengers of our Lord have brought the truth. And the Almighty said: And We sent down iron, in which is great force. That is, We made iron a deterrent to whoever refused the truth and opposed it after the proof had been established against him. For this reason, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, stayed in Mecca for thirteen years after the Prophethood, during which the Meccan surahs were revealed to him, all of which were arguments with the polytheists and clarification and explanation of monotheism, and clear proofs and evidence. When the proof was established against those who opposed it, God prescribed emigration and commanded them to fight with swords and strike the necks and heads of those who opposed the Qur’an, denied it, and opposed it. Imam Ahmad and Abu Dawud narrated from the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Thabit ibn Thauban from Hassan ibn Atiyah from Abu al-Munib al-Jurashi al-Shami from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I was sent with the sword before the Hour so that God alone, with no partner, would be worshipped. My provision was placed under the shade of my spear, and humiliation and degradation were placed upon whoever opposed my command, and whoever imitates a people is one of them.” For this reason, the Almighty said: In it is great force, meaning weapons such as swords, spears, lances, blades, shields, and the like, and benefits for people, that is, in Their livelihoods such as the plow, the axe, the pickaxe, the saw, the chisel, the shovel and the tools that are used in plowing, weaving, cooking, baking, and other things that people cannot live without. Al-Ala’ bin Ahmad said on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas who said: Three things were sent down with Adam: the anvil, the two hooks, and the hammer. This was narrated by Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim. And the saying of God the Almighty: {And that God may know who supports Him and His messengers unseen} meaning of his intention in carrying weapons to support God and His Messenger. {Indeed, God is Powerful and Exalted in Might} meaning He is Powerful and Exalted in Might and He supports whoever supports Him without needing people. And Jihad was only prescribed to test some of you by others.
57:26: God the Almighty informs us that since He sent Noah, peace be upon him, He did not send after him a messenger or prophet except from his descendants. Likewise, Abraham, peace be upon him, the friend of the Most Merciful. No book was sent down from the sky, nor was any messenger sent, nor was any revelation given to any human after him except that he was from his lineage, as God the Almighty said in another verse: And We placed among his descendants prophethood and the Book until the last of the prophets of the Children of Israel was Jesus, son of Mary, who gave good tidings after him of Muhammad, may the peace and blessings of God be upon them both. For this reason, God the Almighty said: Then We followed up their footsteps with Our messengers, and followed up with Jesus, son of Mary, and gave him the Gospel which is the book that God revealed to him and We placed in the hearts of those who followed him and they are the disciples kindness meaning tenderness which is fear and mercy towards creation. And His statement: And monasticism which they innovated meaning the nation of Christians innovated it We did not prescribe it for them meaning We did not legislate it for them, but they adhered to it of their own accord. God the Almighty said: Except seeking the pleasure of God There are two opinions about it. One That they intended thereby to seek the pleasure of God, as stated by Saeed bin Jubair and Qatadah. The other - We did not prescribe that for them, We only prescribe it to seek the pleasure of God. And God the Almighty said: But they did not observe it with its right observance meaning they did not fulfill what they were obligated to do with the right fulfillment. This is a blame on them from two aspects. One - innovating in the religion of God that God did not command, and the second - in their failure to fulfill what they were obligated to do, which they claimed was an act of worship that would bring them closer to God the Almighty. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ishaq bin Abi Hamza Abu Yaqub al-Razi narrated to us, al-Sarri bin Abd Rabbih narrated to us, Bakir bin Maruf narrated to us, from Muqatil bin Hayyan, from al-Qasim bin Abd al-Rahman bin Abdullah bin Masoud, from his father, from his grandfather Ibn Masoud, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to me: O Ibn Masoud. I said: At your service, O Messenger of God. He said: "Did you know that the Children of Israel were divided into seventy-two sects? Only three sects survived. They rose up among the kings and tyrants after Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him. They called to the religion of God and the religion of Jesus, son of Mary. They fought the tyrants and were killed, but they were patient and were saved. Then another group rose up that did not have the strength to fight. They rose up among the kings and tyrants and called to the religion of God and the religion of Jesus, son of Mary. They were killed, cut with saws and burned with fire, but they were patient and were saved. Then another group rose up that did not have the strength to fight and were unable to stand up for justice, so they took to the mountains and worshipped and became monastics. They are the ones about whom God Almighty mentioned: 'And monasticism, which they invented for themselves. We did not prescribe it for them.'" Ibn Jarir narrated it with a different wording from another chain of transmission. He said: Yahya ibn Abi Talib told us, Dawud ibn al-Muhbir told us, al-Sa`q ibn Hazn told us, `Aqil al-Ja`di told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Hamadani, on the authority of Suwayd ibn Ghafla, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn Mas`ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Those who came before us differed into seventy-three sects, three of whom were saved and the rest perished. He mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above, and in it is: So We gave those among them who believed their reward, meaning those who believed in me and believed me. And many of them are wicked, meaning those who denied me and opposed me. This corroboration does not undermine the case of Dawud ibn al-Muhbir, for he is one of the fabricators of hadith. However, Abu Ya`la has attributed it to Shaiban ibn Farukh, on the authority of al-Sa`q ibn Hazn, with something similar to that, so the hadith is strengthened from this aspect. Ibn Jarir and Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Nasa’i said, and the wording is his: Al-Husayn ibn Harith told us, al-Fadl ibn Musa told us, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Sa’id, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: There were kings after Jesus, peace be upon him, and the Torah and the Gospel were changed. There were believers among them who read the Torah and the Gospel. It was said to their kings: We do not find anything more severe than the cursing they curse these people for. They read: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers. These verses, along with what they criticize us for regarding our actions in their reading, so call them, so let them read as we read and believe as we believe. So he called them and gathered them and offered them death or to abandon the reading of the Torah and the Gospel except what they changed from them. They said: What do you want? Let us. A group of them said: Build us a pillar, then raise us to it, then give us something to raise our food and drink with, so that we will not be rejected. A group said: Let us wander in the land and wander and drink as wild animals drink. If you gain power over us in… Your land, so kill us. A group said: Build us houses in the deserts, and we will dig wells and cultivate the vegetables, so that we will not return to you or pass by you. There is no one among the tribes who does not have a close friend among them. So they did that, and God Almighty revealed: “And monasticism, which they invented for themselves. We did not prescribe it for them except seeking the pleasure of God, but they did not observe it with its right observance.” And others said: We will worship as so-and-so worships, and we will travel as so-and-so traveled, and we will take homes as so-and-so did. They were still polytheists and had no knowledge of the faith of those who followed their example. When God sent the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and only a few remained, a man descended from his monastery, a traveler came from his travels, and the owner of the monastery from his monastery. They believed in him and confirmed him. God the Almighty said: “O you who have believed, fear God and believe in His Messenger. He will give you a double portion of His mercy.” They were rewarded for their belief in Jesus, son of Mary, and their belief in the Torah and the Gospel, and for their belief in Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and their confirmation. He said: And He will make for you a light by which you will walk. The Qur’an and their following of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: So that the People of the Scripture who imitate you “will not know that they have no power over any of the bounty of God, and that bounty is in God’s hand. He gives it to whom He wills, and God is the possessor of great bounty.” This context is strange, and the interpretation of these two verses will come later, and God knows best. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili said: Ahmad bin Isa told us, Abdullah bin Wahb told us, Saeed bin Abdul Rahman bin Abi Al-Am’a told me that Sahl bin Abi Umamah told him that he and his father entered upon Anas bin Malik in Madinah during the time of Umar bin Abdul Aziz, who was the governor, and he was praying a short prayer that was like the prayer of a traveler or close to it. When he finished, he said: May God have mercy on you, do you think this is the prescribed prayer or something you are doing without? He said: It is the prescribed prayer and it is the prayer of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). I only made a mistake that I forgot. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to say: “Do not be too hard on yourselves, lest God be hard on you. A people were too hard on themselves, so God was hard on them. Those are the remnants of them in the monasteries and convents, innovating monasticism which We did not prescribe for them.” Then they went out the next day and said: Shall we ride and see and consider? He said: Yes. So they all rode and found themselves in deserted lands whose people had perished, vanished and disappeared, empty on their roofs. They said: Do you recognize these lands? He said: I do not know it or its people. These are the people of the land that were destroyed by oppression and envy. Envy extinguishes the light of good deeds, and oppression confirms or denies that. The eye commits adultery, the hand commits adultery, the foot, the body, the tongue, and the private parts confirm or deny that. Imam Ahmad said: Ya'mar told us, Abdullah told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Zaid al-Ami, on the authority of Abu Iyas, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: For every prophet there is monasticism, and the monasticism of this nation is jihad in the cause of God. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la narrated it on the authority of Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Asma', on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, with the same wording: For every nation there is monasticism, and the monasticism of this nation is jihad in the cause of God. Imam Ahmad said: Husayn told us - he is Ibn Muhammad - Ibn Ayyash, meaning Isma'il, told us on the authority of al-Hajjaj ibn Marwan al-Kila'i and Aqeel ibn Mudrik al-Sulami, on the authority of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri may God be pleased with him that a man came to him and said: Advise me. He said: “You have asked what you asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) before you. I advise you to fear God, for it is the head of everything. You should engage in jihad, for it is the monasticism of Islam. You should remember God and recite the Qur’an, for it is your spirit in the heavens and your remembrance on earth.” Ahmad is the only one to narrate this hadeeth, and God knows best.

The other - We did not prescribe that for them, We only prescribe it to seek the pleasure of God. And God the Almighty said: But they did not observe it with its right observance meaning they did not fulfill what they were obligated to do with the right fulfillment. This is a blame on them from two aspects. One - innovating in the religion of God that God did not command, and the second - in their failure to fulfill what they were obligated to do, which they claimed was an act of worship that would bring them closer to God the Almighty. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ishaq bin Abi Hamza Abu Yaqub al-Razi narrated to us, al-Sarri bin Abd Rabbih narrated to us, Bakir bin Maruf narrated to us, from Muqatil bin Hayyan, from al-Qasim bin Abd al-Rahman bin Abdullah bin Masoud, from his father, from his grandfather Ibn Masoud, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to me: O Ibn Masoud. I said: At your service, O Messenger of God. He said: "Did you know that the Children of Israel were divided into seventy-two sects? Only three sects survived. They rose up among the kings and tyrants after Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him. They called to the religion of God and the religion of Jesus, son of Mary. They fought the tyrants and were killed, but they were patient and were saved. Then another group rose up that did not have the strength to fight. They rose up among the kings and tyrants and called to the religion of God and the religion of Jesus, son of Mary. They were killed, cut with saws and burned with fire, but they were patient and were saved. Then another group rose up that did not have the strength to fight and were unable to stand up for justice, so they took to the mountains and worshipped and became monastics. They are the ones about whom God Almighty mentioned: 'And monasticism, which they invented for themselves. We did not prescribe it for them.'" Ibn Jarir narrated it with a different wording from another chain of transmission. He said: Yahya ibn Abi Talib told us, Dawud ibn al-Muhbir told us, al-Sa`q ibn Hazn told us, `Aqil al-Ja`di told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Hamadani, on the authority of Suwayd ibn Ghafla, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn Mas`ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Those who came before us differed into seventy-three sects, three of whom were saved and the rest perished. He mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above, and in it is: So We gave those among them who believed their reward, meaning those who believed in me and believed me. And many of them are wicked, meaning those who denied me and opposed me. This corroboration does not undermine the case of Dawud ibn al-Muhbir, for he is one of the fabricators of hadith. However, Abu Ya`la has attributed it to Shaiban ibn Farukh, on the authority of al-Sa`q ibn Hazn, with something similar to that, so the hadith is strengthened from this aspect. Ibn Jarir and Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Nasa’i said, and the wording is his: Al-Husayn ibn Harith told us, al-Fadl ibn Musa told us, on the authority of Sufyan ibn Sa’id, on the authority of Ata’ ibn al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: There were kings after Jesus, peace be upon him, and the Torah and the Gospel were changed. There were believers among them who read the Torah and the Gospel. It was said to their kings: We do not find anything more severe than the cursing they curse these people for. They read: And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed - then it is those who are the disbelievers. These verses, along with what they criticize us for regarding our actions in their reading, so call them, so let them read as we read and believe as we believe. So he called them and gathered them and offered them death or to abandon the reading of the Torah and the Gospel except what they changed from them. They said: What do you want? Let us. A group of them said: Build us a pillar, then raise us to it, then give us something to raise our food and drink with, so that we will not be rejected. A group said: Let us wander in the land and wander and drink as wild animals drink. If you gain power over us in… Your land, so kill us. A group said: Build us houses in the deserts, and we will dig wells and cultivate the vegetables, so that we will not return to you or pass by you. There is no one among the tribes who does not have a close friend among them. So they did that, and God Almighty revealed: “And monasticism, which they invented for themselves. We did not prescribe it for them except seeking the pleasure of God, but they did not observe it with its right observance.” And others said: We will worship as so-and-so worships, and we will travel as so-and-so traveled, and we will take homes as so-and-so did. They were still polytheists and had no knowledge of the faith of those who followed their example. When God sent the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and only a few remained, a man descended from his monastery, a traveler came from his travels, and the owner of the monastery from his monastery. They believed in him and confirmed him. God the Almighty said: “O you who have believed, fear God and believe in His Messenger. He will give you a double portion of His mercy.” They were rewarded for their belief in Jesus, son of Mary, and their belief in the Torah and the Gospel, and for their belief in Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and their confirmation. He said: And He will make for you a light by which you will walk. The Qur’an and their following of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: So that the People of the Scripture who imitate you “will not know that they have no power over any of the bounty of God, and that bounty is in God’s hand. He gives it to whom He wills, and God is the possessor of great bounty.” This context is strange, and the interpretation of these two verses will come later, and God knows best. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la Al-Mawsili said: Ahmad bin Isa told us, Abdullah bin Wahb told us, Saeed bin Abdul Rahman bin Abi Al-Am’a told me that Sahl bin Abi Umamah told him that he and his father entered upon Anas bin Malik in Madinah during the time of Umar bin Abdul Aziz, who was the governor, and he was praying a short prayer that was like the prayer of a traveler or close to it. When he finished, he said: May God have mercy on you, do you think this is the prescribed prayer or something you are doing without? He said: It is the prescribed prayer and it is the prayer of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). I only made a mistake that I forgot. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) used to say: “Do not be too hard on yourselves, lest God be hard on you. A people were too hard on themselves, so God was hard on them. Those are the remnants of them in the monasteries and convents, innovating monasticism which We did not prescribe for them.” Then they went out the next day and said: Shall we ride and see and consider? He said: Yes. So they all rode and found themselves in deserted lands whose people had perished, vanished and disappeared, empty on their roofs. They said: Do you recognize these lands? He said: I do not know it or its people. These are the people of the land that were destroyed by oppression and envy. Envy extinguishes the light of good deeds, and oppression confirms or denies that. The eye commits adultery, the hand commits adultery, the foot, the body, the tongue, and the private parts confirm or deny that. Imam Ahmad said: Ya'mar told us, Abdullah told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Zaid al-Ami, on the authority of Abu Iyas, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: For every prophet there is monasticism, and the monasticism of this nation is jihad in the cause of God. Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la narrated it on the authority of Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Asma', on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, with the same wording: For every nation there is monasticism, and the monasticism of this nation is jihad in the cause of God. Imam Ahmad said: Husayn told us - he is Ibn Muhammad - Ibn Ayyash, meaning Isma'il, told us on the authority of al-Hajjaj ibn Marwan al-Kila'i and Aqeel ibn Mudrik al-Sulami, on the authority of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri may God be pleased with him that a man came to him and said: Advise me. He said: “You have asked what you asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) before you. I advise you to fear God, for it is the head of everything. You should engage in jihad, for it is the monasticism of Islam. You should remember God and recite the Qur’an, for it is your spirit in the heavens and your remembrance on earth.” Ahmad is the only one to narrate this hadeeth, and God knows best.
57:28: It was mentioned in the narration of al-Nasa’i on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he applied this verse to the believers among the People of the Book and that they will be given their reward twice, as in the verse in Al-Qasas and as in the hadith of Al-Sha’bi on the authority of Abu Burdah on the authority of his father on the authority of Abu Musa Al-Ash’ari, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There are three who will be given their reward twice: a man among the People of the Book who believed in his Prophet and believed in me, so he will have two rewards; a slave who fulfilled the right of God and the right of his masters, so he will have two rewards; and a man who disciplined his female slave and disciplined her well, then freed her and married her, so he will have two rewards.” They included it in the two Sahihs. Ad-Dahhak, Utbah bin Abi Hakim, and others agreed with Ibn Abbas on this interpretation, and it is the choice of Ibn Jarir. Sa’id bin Jubayr said: When the People of the Book boasted that they will be given their reward twice, God Almighty revealed this verse to him regarding this nation: “O you who have believed, fear God and believe in His Messenger. He will give you a double portion” meaning twice of His mercy and and He will increase them and and He will make for you a light by which you will walk. “It means guidance by which you can see from blindness and ignorance and forgive you. So He favored them with light and forgiveness. Narrated by Ibn Jarir on his authority. This verse is like the saying of God the Almighty: “O you who have believed, if you fear God, He will grant you a criterion and remove from you your misdeeds and forgive you. And God is the possessor of great bounty.” Sa’id ibn Abd al-Aziz said: Umar ibn al-Khattab asked one of the Jewish rabbis: How much is the best of what you have doubled as a good deed? He said: It is equal to three hundred and fifty good deeds. Umar then praised God for giving us two parts, then Sa’id mentioned the saying of God the Almighty: He will give you a double portion of His mercy. Sa’id said: The two portions on Friday are the same. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. What supports this statement is what Imam Ahmad narrated: Ismail told us, Ayoub told us, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Your example and that of the Jews and Christians is like that of a man who hired workers and said, ‘Who will work for me from the dawn prayer until noon for one qirat, one qirat?’ So the Jews worked. Then he said, ‘Who will work for me from the noon prayer until the afternoon prayer for one qirat, one qirat?’ So the Christians worked. Then he said, ‘Who will work for me from the afternoon prayer until sunset for two qirats, two qirats?’ So you are the ones who worked. The Christians and Jews became angry and said, ‘We work more and are paid less.’ He said, ‘Have I wronged you in any way regarding your reward?’ They said, ‘No.’ He said, ‘It is only My bounty which I give to whomever I wish.’” Ahmad said: Muammil narrated to us from Sufyan from Abdullah bin Dinar from Ibn Umar something similar to the hadith of Nafi’ from him. Al-Bukhari alone transmitted it. He narrated it from Sulayman bin Harb from Hammad from Nafi’ with it, and from Qutaybah from Al-Layth from Nafi’ with a similar hadith. Al-Bukhari said: Muhammad bin Al-Ala’ narrated to me, Abu Usamah narrated to us from Burayd from Abu Burdah from Abu Musa from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The example of the Muslims, Jews, and Christians is like that of a man who employs people to do work for him from day to night for a known wage. They work until midday, then they say: We have no need of the wage you stipulated for us, and what we do is in vain. He said to them: Do not do that. Complete the rest of your work and take your full wage. They refused and left. Then he hired others after them and said: Complete the rest of your day and you will have the wage you stipulated for them. So they worked until the time for the ‘Asr prayer came, and they said: What we did was in vain, and you will have the wage you promised us for it. He said: Complete the rest of your work, for only a little of the day remains, but they refused. So he hired some people to work for him for the rest of their day, and they worked.” He had the rest of their day until sunset, and they completed the reward of both groups. This is their example and the example of what they accepted from this light. This was reported only by Al-Bukhari. That is why God Almighty said: So that the People of the Scripture may know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of God meaning, so that they may realize that they are not able to return what God has given them or give what God has withheld. And that bounty is in God’s hand; He gives it to whom He wills. “And God is the possessor of great bounty.” Ibn Jarir said, So that the People of the Book may know, meaning so that he may know. It was reported that Ibn Masoud recited it so that he may know, as did Hattan ibn Abdullah and Saeed ibn Jubayr. Ibn Jarir said, “Because the Arabs add ‘la’ to every statement that has a denial at the beginning or end that is not explicitly stated. So the previous one is like His saying, ‘What prevented you from prostrating?’ ‘And what makes you perceive that, when it comes, they will not believe’ in God, ‘And it is forbidden for a city which We have destroyed that they will not return.’” End of the interpretation of Surat Al-Hadid. All praise and thanks are due to God.
